notes: All 219 source JSON files were checked; these are the 10 with relevant=true and army_family=super-minion-air. Support counts distinct videos, including their rules and policies, rather than attacks within a video.

The selected complete army is shared by HnEtYULN4Y0 and dn6J46bW0ts after flattening the former's nested Clan Castle fields. Every other quantified composition differs. This is the most frequent complete composition, not a majority of all 10 videos or a vote on individual equipment items.

Wiki: Workshop, only one Siege Machine can be used per battle. HnEtYULN4Y0 and dn6J46bW0ts list Flame Flinger, Stone Slammer, Troop Launcher, Siege Barracks and Log Launcher as available options. The default army selects only Flame Flinger; the other four are not camp troops or Clan Castle cargo. Log Launcher and Troop Launcher variants require that selected siege in the supplied build. The Battle Drill variant requires pTmX2vmv4sc's alternative inventory.

Initial Healer deployment is not explicitly narrated in any extraction. The five Healers remain in the inventory without an invented deployment step. A complete shared deployment sequence for the main Super Minions is also absent; unquantified funnel and late-support drops have not been converted into numerical allocations or an all-troops drop.

The Dragon Duke deployment is supported only by pTmX2vmv4sc's conditional plan to push King, Queen and Duke toward the Town Hall if the Warden survives and maintains his route. inside:Grand Warden is the closest available proxy for that living Warden continuing into the base. Other sources mainly describe the Duke's ability without a deployment step.

t=0 translates the opening Warden deployment. Every delay=0 encodes narrated order when no delay is stated. Caption timestamps are citation times, not attack-relative deployment times. The sources vary on whether Flame Flinger or Warden is placed first; concurrent opening work is approximated by ordered zero-delay steps.

Fireball setup is incomplete in the available vocabulary: O8of3SqwmUo, dn6J46bW0ts and qlLv2Bvu4ig describe one- or two-Invisibility setups, while 12Z_sTAEOHw also describes three or four with Ice Block. The buildings to hide and portable placement coordinates are not specified sufficiently for executable redirection casts. No casting interval is stated.

Recall timing varies: some sources immediately recall after Fireball, while others first remove additional defenses or continue until danger. Those building-destruction and desired-value conditions have no matching trigger. The default after-fireball zero-delay trigger collapses the unquantified extra walk; the continued-walk variant approximates danger with heavy_fire.

edge:main represents the scouted hero entry, edge:charge the opening Warden flank, and edge:funnel the second flank. The redeployed Warden uses edge:funnel as a proxy for the separately chosen safe second position; absolute clock positions and an independent third entry cannot be preserved with these anchors.

Hero-ability activation order, Giant Arrow angles, Rocket Backpack angles and Fireball aiming geometry are incompletely narrated. The zero-delay ability sequence supplies ordering only; the unit anchors do not encode an aiming line.

The King trigger after wall_breakers approximates a completed funnel and opened entry, which have no direct completion trigger. inside:Barbarian King approximates reaching the core for Spiky Ball. heavy_fire:Archer Queen approximates the narrated need for Druid healing without inventing a health percentage. The Druid misses the intended Queen in x5AiCcU008Y's demonstrated example.

The initial Ice Golem precedes the Queen to approximate the narrated tanking role. The release-siege variant uses inside:Archer Queen as the closest trigger to releasing reinforcements in front of her. The early Spiky Ball variant uses after:king with zero delay because the remaining Ice Golem freeze duration is not stated.

defenders_near includes defending heroes as well as Clan Castle troops; it is the closest available trigger for the cited Headhunter and Furnace Clan Castle threats. The source-specific identities are more precise than the executor's trigger.

The five Wall Breakers come from HnEtYULN4Y0's max-wall instruction and dn6J46bW0ts's explicit five-Wall-Breaker Queen entry. The latter pairs the entry with Invisibility but does not identify that spell's target, so no additional placement is asserted.

The inventory's five Earthquakes do not establish a common casting sequence. Explicit alternatives include three on the Revenge Tower/core and two split over the Revenge Tower and Monolith. Three casts are separate steps because no repeat interval is supplied. The split casts share a trigger to represent simultaneous placement.

The one-Super-Minion charge variant maps an unquantified lengthy-charge or time-pressure stage to after:warden with zero delay. The two-Super-Minion sniper variant maps late cleanup to after:king_spiky_ball and uses edge:funnel as the closest deploy-edge anchor to the selected remaining Super Wizard Tower; exact sniping tiles are absent.

The same-side Flame Flinger variant waits for Fireball as a proxy for the narrated extra Warden clearing, including removal of an X-Bow. The Troop Launcher follows the described hero-ability sequence. Battle Drill deployment timing is unstated and uses the shared post-Fireball siege stage with zero delay.

Variants describe alternative phases, not a set to apply simultaneously. The Royal Champion/Rage and Ice Block variants require the corresponding source army and loadouts; the default inventory has neither Royal Champion, Rage Spell nor Ice Block Spell. No fixed spell cadence is supplied.

12Z_sTAEOHw is a Town Hall 16 Fireball/Rocket Balloon plan against Town Hall 18 bases, grouped here because its Flame Flinger carries Super Minions. Its alternative has 11 Rocket Balloons, 5 Healers, 2 Furnaces, 2 Ice Golems and no trained Super Minions; spells are Rage 1, Earthquake 2, Invisibility 5, Ice Block 1 and Poison 1. Its Clan Castle includes Super Minion 4, Minion 1, Recall 1 and Totem 1. It uses Royal Champion with Seeking Shield, Rocket Spear and Diggy instead of Dragon Duke; King has Earthquake Boots/Spiky Ball, Queen Magic Mirror/Action Figure, and Warden Rage Gem/Fireball. Its King can use Spiky Ball before the Queen entry, and its recall can leave a Healer behind when Unicorn survives.

pTmX2vmv4sc's alternative has 6 Super Minions, 8 Rocket Balloons, 5 Healers, 3 Furnaces, 1 Ice Golem and 2 Druids. Its link lists Invisibility 4, Earthquake 5 and Totem 2; narrated Freeze, Poison and Recall quantities are unresolved, and Clan Castle contents are unspecified. Siege choices include Flame Flinger, Troop Launcher and Battle Drill, with a separately narrated Log Launcher approach. King uses Stick Horse and Warden Greedy Raven. The narrator replaces Revive with additional Freeze and Invisibility because the revived Duke otherwise lacks support.

qlLv2Bvu4ig's Town Hall 18 alternative has 8 Super Minions, 8 Rocket Balloons, 5 Healers, 3 Furnaces, 1 Ice Golem and 1 Druid; spells are Invisibility 3, Earthquake 5, Poison 1 and Revive 1. Its Clan Castle has Super Yeti 1, Super Valkyrie 1, Recall 1 and Totem 2. King uses Stick Horse and Warden Greedy Raven. Its guide permits same-side Warden/Flinger funneling when removing the core would otherwise let the heroes split.

tFITZCY8XhU's alternative has 5 Super Minions, 9 Rocket Balloons, 5 Healers, 2 Furnaces, 2 Ice Golems, 1 Yeti and 2 Druids; spells are Invisibility 3, Earthquake 5, Poison 1 and Revive 1, with Recall 1 and Totem 2 in the Clan Castle. The full siege payload is unresolved. King uses Stick Horse, Warden Greedy Raven and Duke Revenge Deck/Rocket Backpack. Its examples include manually releasing Flame Flinger reinforcements and reviving the Warden.

yiUwu_vHfng's Town Hall 13 alternative has 6 Super Minions, 11 Rocket Balloons, 5 Healers and 2 Ice Golems; spells are Earthquake 2, Invisibility 3, Poison 1, Rage 1, Skeleton 1 and Freeze 2. Its Clan Castle contains Flame Flinger 1, Super Minion 3, Rocket Balloon 1, Barbarian 1 and Recall 1. Heroes are King with Spiky Ball/Stick Horse, Queen with Action Figure/Magic Mirror, Warden with Rage Gem/Fireball, and Royal Champion with Rocket Spear/Electro Boots. Recall is discussed but no cast is established in that extraction.

O8of3SqwmUo, b_kCBBnsuvo and x5AiCcU008Y provide partial inventories with unknown totals, so they do not supply another complete composition. x5AiCcU008Y explicitly has three Headhunters and three Invisibility Spells. O8of3SqwmUo favors Troop Launcher in several examples, while other sources also discuss Log Launcher or omitting Flame Flinger when X-Bows or defending heroes restrict it.

Revive is contested and absent from the selected army. qlLv2Bvu4ig, b_kCBBnsuvo and x5AiCcU008Y describe reviving Dragon Duke; O8of3SqwmUo discusses reserving it. pTmX2vmv4sc argues against it without follow-up spells, and tFITZCY8XhU revives Warden instead. No revival target or corpse-position anchor has been invented.

The '1 minute 30-ish' hero timing in dn6J46bW0ts does not identify elapsed versus remaining time and is not converted into a numeric trigger. Unresolved names such as cake, candle, logger and long shot remain unresolved. Failed or criticized placements, including unsuccessful Warden pulls, are not promoted to default rules.
Steps marked completion: true were added from the source transcripts for units the consolidated playbook never deployed (docs/playbook-completion.md, merge_completion.py).
